title: 3.8.0 low batch
description: D9: every open register low scheduled for 3.8.0 and every carried P143 review finding (BUG-31-z9j), grouped one task per file cluster with one shared fix per recurring class. Plan: quality-gates-internal/plans/2026-11-02-low-batch-3-8-0.md.
desiredOutcome: Every open low scheduled for 3.8.0 is fixed or closed with a reason, and BUG-31-z9j is closed

findings.issue: No case covers the new refusal of an --answer sent to a set-aside sign-off decision. rf1/rf2 cover only the no-answer path: dispatch, and the blocked twin. If lines 9408-9411 are deleted, most answers are still refused, but by answer_refusal's different 'no decision is pending' text. `--answer sign-off --reason` would instead take _pending_route's advance route (pending is None) and drive on. The PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE sentence claiming the refusal cites rf1/rf2, and neither case reaches it.
findings.resolution: Add a case (rf12): with the drive at the triage, add a task with the verb, then run `next --answer sign-off --reason S`. Assert exit 2, the added task's id in the text, no pending left in state, and the phase not signed off. Cite it beside the guide sentence.

findings.issue: decline_answer's docstring says 'The drive goes on to any task still open - the remedy a human added', and db2 pins that by calling decline_answer directly. Through `next`, a human who adds the remedy task first and then answers `--answer decline --reason <words>` is now refused at drive_locked:9408, because the decision is set aside while the remedy is ready. Their words never reach state['declined'], so the summary loses the no. That branch of decline_answer is now reachable only for an open task that cannot run. DECLINE_REMEDY's order (decline first, then add) still works.
findings.resolution: Either let `decline` through on a set-aside decision (record the words in `declined`, pop phaseGate, then drive the runnable task), or reword the docstring and db2 so they describe an open task that cannot run. Add a drive-level case for whichever is chosen.

findings.issue: _status_facts.unmet_refs already folds a blocked phase's refs into each task's entry as '<ref> (phase)' (_status_facts.py:1424). not_ready_why then appends unmet[phase_id] a second time. A wave member dropped because its phase gained a blocker therefore prints that ref twice in the dropped-from-wave line: 'waits on P9 (phase), P9'.
findings.resolution: Read unmet.get(task_id) alone, since it already carries the phase's refs, and fall back to 'nothing the plan names' only when it is empty.

findings.issue: The task widens the ruff path list in tools/verify.sh to include .claude/hooks, but CLAUDE.md:210 (the 'Tests' command block, 'the commands a change most often reruns by hand') and the plan's meta.buildCommands.lint still spell `ruff check plugins/audit tools tests`. A contributor or a build-command-driven gate following either runs a narrower ruff than verify.sh and would not see an unused import under .claude/hooks - the very class this task closes. The executor reported this as left for the orchestrator; it is a changed shape crossing into untouched files.
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.17-gfj (fa53e61bae2a): Add `.claude/hooks` to the ruff line at CLAUDE.md:210 and set meta.buildCommands.lint through `/audit:task build-command` (or drop the hand copy and point at `verify.sh --list`).

findings.issue: The diff edits two files the task does not declare, plugins/audit/reference/verbs-in-full.md and plugins/audit/README.md. It also declares plugins/audit/commands/verbs-in-full.md, which does not exist: the recorded gate run's scopeBasis reads '17 declared file(s); 16 read, 1 missing'. This has two consequences. (a) This is the 1-of-292 test__refs failure in the red-first fix run. That run takes only the declared implementation files from the working tree. So task.md's argument-hint, which now has --gate-add (it is declared and was copied), met HEAD's plugins/audit/README.md, which lacks it: `git show c2c057fd:plugins/audit/README.md | grep -c -- --gate-add` gives 0. That pair is exactly what test__refs cf1 (`command_flag_drift`, tests/test__refs.py:2164-2168) compares. This is an inference from reading, not from re-running test__refs. The recorded gate run 2026-11-02T09:48:08Z.c4ebb4, on the full task tree (head c2c057fd, the same dirtyDigest), passed test__refs with exit 0. So the failure comes from the scope mismatch and not from a defect in the code. (b) commit-task-work's `_scoped_commit.undeclared_changes` (commit-task-work.py:692-713) will refuse the task commit over the two undeclared paths.
findings.resolution: Run `/audit:task scope P155.6 --files +plugins/audit/reference/verbs-in-full.md,plugins/audit/README.md`, then record the gate again. If the stale `plugins/audit/commands/verbs-in-full.md` entry is dropped, the red-first helper's fix run copies the README too, and can then prove or refuse on the merits.

findings.issue: This is a user-visible change to a shipped verb, and neither the changelog nor the compatibility record mentions it. `audit-task.py scope <id> --gate Y` on a task whose tests.gate holds entries Y leaves out used to exit 0 and replace the list. It now exits 2 and writes nothing (`_scope_gate_refusal`, audit-task.py:10207-10244). New behaviour: `--gate-add`, the success-line clause 'tests.gate now holds [...]', and the `gateNowHolds` key in --json. COMPATIBILITY.md's contract covers the manifest and the config only, and `--gate` is still read, so no promise is broken. But the document records every earlier exit-code move on an audit-task verb 'because an exit code moved from 0 to 2 on a shipped command, and a pipeline that read ... is a pipeline that now stops' (COMPATIBILITY.md:546-556). The repo's precedent P153-R3 filed the missing CHANGELOG line for a `--gate*` behaviour change as a finding. No caller inside the repo is broken: commands, agents, skills, the drive (drive-phase.py only builds `scope --files` argvs, :3203 and :6817), tools, examples and .github build no `scope --gate` argv, and the suite's own replace-meaning callers (sn4, gc3, jf, fg1, fg3, dg4b, gx1) now pass --replace.
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.18-gfj (59537230ae88): Scope CHANGELOG.md and COMPATIBILITY.md into the task. Add an [Unreleased] '### Changed' entry: `scope --gate` refuses a list that leaves out a held entry unless --replace (exit 2, nothing written). Add an '### Added' entry for `--gate-add` and `gateNowHolds`. Add a COMPATIBILITY.md not-promised bullet, in the shape of the existing 'which FLAGS a verb accepts ... and it changed' entry, naming the exit-code move and the repair (`--replace`, or `--gate-add`).

findings.issue: The validator's wide-gate warning fires when a task's tests.gate is its phase's testGate verbatim. It tells the operator to 'Narrow it to the paths this task names ... go through `/audit:task scope <id> --gate "<command>"`'. A narrowed list leaves out held entries by definition, so after this diff that exact call is refused without --replace. This file is outside the diff, but the diff changed the verb on the other side of that instruction. The executor disclosed this, and the plan gate refused the edit. The refusal names --replace, so the cost is one round trip.
findings.resolution: Scope _manifest_phases.py, and tests/test__manifest_phases.py if a case pins the text, into this task or a follow-up. Say that narrowing takes `--gate "<command>" --replace`, while declaring the wide gate as the answer (the same list, which drops nothing) still takes a bare `--gate`.

findings.issue: `--gate-add Y` on a task that declares no gate of its own writes `[Y]` with gateBasis `declared`. Such a task has tests.gate absent, `[]` or all-blank, gateBasis not `cleared`, and `_mio.gate_entries` (_manifest_io.py:663-692) measures it by the phase's testGate. So the gate that grades the task silently shrinks from the phase's entries to `[Y]`. Yet the help text, task.md and verbs-in-full describe --gate-add as appending 'keeping every entry the task holds'. `_held_gate` and `_gate_added` read only the stored list, never the resolved one. This is the class this task closes: a call spelled as 'keep' loses entries the gate ran. The success line prints `[Y]` but not what it replaced.
findings.resolution: In `_locked_scope`, when `_held_gate(node)` is empty and `_mio.gate_entries(phase, node)` returns source 'phase' with entries, do one of two things. Either refuse `--gate-add`, naming the phase gate it would replace and the spelling that keeps it (`--gate <each phase entry> --gate Y`), or seed the append with those resolved entries. Add a gk case on such a task that tells the two outcomes apart.

findings.issue: The commit's count of 'declared' got wider, but what it stages did not. owned_rels now counts every fileIndex row keyed to the committing task. stage_targets still stages only task.files (commit-task-work.py:355-376). So a changed path that only a fileIndex row of the task names lands in undeclared_changes' `covered` (_scoped_commit.py:1507-1514). The commit treats it as work in flight: it does not refuse it and does not stage it. The file stays dirty and the task closes `done` without it. Before this diff the commit refused that path by name; now it drops it in silence, the outcome attempt_refusal's own docstring says it exists to prevent. The validator allows such rows: _manifest_crossrefs._check_file_index only requires files to be a subset of fileIndex, not the reverse. dp1 asserts the commit 'counts' src/indexed.py but never asserts the path is committed. Found by reading, not by a run.
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.19-gfj (cd857887694b): Treat `files` alone as declared. fileIndex is derived from files (`audit-task.py reindex`), so a row present only in fileIndex is drift: declared_task_map should not read fileIndex rows that no counted task's files covers. The hook then denies more, never less. Update dp1's expected list (src/indexed.py is neither opened nor counted). If fileIndex rows must stay, stage_targets has to stage every declared_task_map entry of the committing task. Either way, add a case: a path only the committing task's fileIndex row names is committed or refused, never left dirty after `done`.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "Closes F818" (F818 Do / tests.add: submit 'refuses with the scope remedy (or the return carries the widened list and scope-changed is asked once)', 'while the executor is still there', not after the review round). On the wave path a member's undeclared edit is only appended to a did-line. The filed return carries no widened list and no reason, and no decision is raised. The question is first asked by integrate_member's undeclared-change decision (:4432). That runs after the reviewer is dispatched (:4416) and after the risk confirmation. For wave members, F818's defect is unchanged: the change is found after the review round, and the orchestrator answers it without the executor's reason.
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.20-gfj (578cfd35a657): For a member, record the strays submit_strays found in the drive state (or in the filed return, with the executor's reason). Make the step after the member's gate ask undeclared-change or scope-changed for those paths before the reviewer is dispatched, leaving out the paths the gate row's followersOwed names (integration widens those). Keep sd4's assertion that the member is filed, and add a case: the decision about the stray comes before `dispatch reviewer`.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "The executor brief names the PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md section per declared module." The diff contains no change to brief generation. The executor's outcome says so and gives the reason: audit-lookup.py is not in the task's files. F818 is therefore not closed by this diff, but the description says 'Closes F818'.
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.21-gfj (897247de22e5): Either widen the scope to plugins/audit/scripts/status/audit-lookup.py and its suite and implement the clause, or split it into a follow-up task and record F818 as open in the register for that half.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "Closes F808" (F808 Do: 'the dry run made in the tree after setup'). recut_conflicts still checks a three-way apply against the bare phase head. The real apply (:6362) runs in a tree that add_tree has already put through executor.worktreeSetup. A setup that rewrites a tracked file still fails after the old tree was kept. findings.file: plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py:4011-4016; plugins/audit/scripts/governance/commit-task-work.py:616-619; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (added _config paragraph: 'a path the plan gate opened to an edit is never one the task commit refuses as undeclared')
findings.issue: contradicts task clause "Closes F808" (Do (a): 'the plan gate and commit-task-work read one predicate for "declared"'). The plan gate has a second reading of declared, which the shared predicate leaves out. require-plan.py:970-974 allows an edit as a 'declared output of in_progress task' via task_covered_outputs. Neither declared_task_map nor owned_rels reads `outputs`. So a path a task's graded outputs pattern covers is opened by the gate, then refused by the commit as 'changed during this attempt and no in_progress task declares it', one gate run late. findings.resolution: fixed in P155.23-gfj (198cab9c48f3): Have the commit's reading count the counted tasks' graded outputs (_config.in_progress_outputs, or an `outputs` arm in declared_git_rels passed to undeclared_changes), and add a dp case where one outputs path is opened by the gate and counted by the commit. If outputs are meant to stay outside the commit, rewrite the three sentences so they name outputs (and the free-file slot) as outside the shared predicate.

findings.issue: redo_pin_spent counts a blocked task as spent even when its patch still stands. Blocked is not terminal: `unblock` returns the task to pending. When the task is next stepped, redo_left calls redo_held, which can no longer resolve the pin ('names no commit'), so it answers 'could not be read'. The stop then tells the human to compare against `<pin>^` and `<pin>`, refs this diff has deleted. The redo_left docstring describes the pin as the second copy of work 'which may be its only copy'.
findings.resolution: Make it `status in _mio.TERMINAL or not patch_stands`, so a blocked task keeps its pin while its patch stands. sd11 has no patch, so it stays green. Or, in the arm where the pin is gone, word the 'could not be read' remedy without the pin.

findings.issue: In sd9, sd10 and sd11 no patch is written, so in each case `not patch_stands` alone makes redo_pin_spent true. The status arm (TERMINAL, blocked) never decides a case. From reading, the mutation `return not patch_stands` would leave sd9-sd13 green; the probe's m6/m7 do not try it. The clause 'gone after done, cancel, block' is proved only for tasks that have no patch.
findings.resolution: Add a case where a patch still stands on a done or cancelled task, and assert the pin is gone. Probe it with the mutation `return not patch_stands`.

findings.issue: The window is written to $WORKDIR/live-window/audit-plan.json, outside any checkout, so render-report resolves its project through _output.project_of_manifest to /tmp/verify-*/live-window (markerless fallback; checked in memory: project_of_manifest('/tmp/verify-XYZ/live-window/audit-plan.json') -> '/tmp/verify-XYZ/live-window'). The committed evidence ledger (docs/audit/evidence) is then never read. Measured in memory with _evidence_view.load_evidence on the same manifest: at the checkout path, keys ['passed','failed','empty-gate','no-evidence'], flags ['tree-mutated','tree-unknown','no-overlap','coverage-unknown','checks-unknown'], files 60. At the window path, keys ['dangling','no-evidence'], flags [], files 0. So the leg now drives a report where every pointer is 'dangling', a status the real plan never shows, and it loses every real evidence status and flag. That was what made the live-plan leg the report that 'DOES carry evidence' (tools/check-report-interactive.mjs:766-770). Nothing goes red: validate-manifest passes and the browser check accepts either page. The new comment ('the page still shows each key and status the plan uses') and CONTRIBUTING.md:503-504 overclaim for the same reason. The project's .claude/audit.config.json (theme and panel config) is also no longer read.
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.24-gfj (22585b1d033e): Give the window a project the renderer resolves the way it resolves the checkout. Write it under a record-shaped path, $WORKDIR/live-window/docs/audit/audit-plan.json, so the project is $WORKDIR/live-window. Copy docs/audit/evidence/ (and .claude/audit.config.json) beside it. Then make the drift fail: after the render, assert that the window's load_evidence keys and flags equal the full plan's (or, at minimum, contain no 'dangling' the full plan lacks) and fail the leg otherwise.

findings.issue: The fixed count `20` of recent done phases carries no basis. The comment calls it only 'the third argument'. Running the selection in memory on today's plan gives: not-done 6, recent +20, shape arm +2, reference closure +19, total 47 of 158. So the 20 is the largest single share of the window. It adds no key or status, since the shape arm already guarantees those, so its only effect is size. Nothing says what a recent done phase exercises that the other arms do not, or why 20 rather than 5.
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.30-gfj (c9520404a393): State in the comment what the recent done phases exist for (e.g. the merged/review/sign-off surfaces of recently merged phases) and why that count covers it. Or derive the count from that property instead of a literal. Otherwise drop the arm and let the shape arm and the closure decide.

findings.issue: shape() reads only top-level phase and task keys, so nested shapes the full plan holds are dropped silently. In memory the window loses task.outcome.filesTouched and task.outcome.summary (the legacy object form of outcome, a distinct render branch) and task.tests.falsifiers. CONTRIBUTING.md says 'The window keeps every phase and task key and status the plan uses', which is true only of top-level keys.
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.30-gfj (c9520404a393): Extend shape() one level into dict-valued phase and task keys (('task.outcome', k) etc.), or narrow the CONTRIBUTING sentence and the comment to 'top-level key'.

findings.issue: Inherited-test shape: the task's gate entry `sh tools/verify.sh --list` sets LIST=1, and `run "rendered-plan legs ..." rendered_plan_legs` then prints the step name without executing the function. So no command in tests.gate reaches the window heredoc. Deleting its closure, its proposal filter or its shape arm leaves both gate commands green. The executor's red demonstrations were scratch copies, not a recorded check. (This is from reading verify.sh, not from a run.)
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.25-gfj (e88eb3e0278f): Move the window selection into a stdlib tools/ script with a tests/ suite. Run it against a fixture plan holding a cross-phase dependsOn, a materialized proposal, a bug on a dropped task and a phase with a unique key, and assert closure, filtering and shape-set equality. Proving red is part of the case.

findings.issue: restore_copy can write over newer work at a path the copy holds. It drops every path in `held` from `_newer_work`'s answer (`[p for p in _newer_work(...) if p not in held]`), and `_undo` then `_put`s each held path unconditionally. Suppose a.txt is a held work path and, after the kill, someone (a human, or a writer session that was already running) edits it to bytes that are neither the copy's nor `start`'s nor `end`'s. The restore overwrites that edit without saying so. un7 covers only an unheld path (c.txt), so this direction has no test. The docstring narrows the contract to 'the paths it holds are what a restore is asked to write over', which conflicts with 'never write over newer work'.
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.26-gfj (32b4ca49159c): Before `_undo`, refuse any held path whose bytes match none of these: the copy (`_holds(tree, rel, held[rel])`), `start`'s blob, or `end`'s blob (`_reads_as`, absent where the commit has none). Those are the only states a killed move or a killed undo can leave. un6's tree (a.txt at base, n.txt absent) still passes. Add a case like un7 that edits a.txt and expects a refusal with nothing changed.

findings.issue: `hash-object --no-filters` costs more than the docstring says. With core.autocrlf=true, the Git for Windows installer default, every text file checkout writes with CRLF hashes differently from its LF blob. So a move killed partway through its checkout leaves moved paths that `_newer_work` reads as newer work. The resume holds the tree, and so does the restore verb the new stop names: restore_copy runs the same `_newer_work` and refuses those paths, because moved paths are not in `held`. On a default Windows checkout, the stop's sentence '`restore` puts the work back from it and takes it down' is then false and no verb can settle the tree. The filtered hash this replaces accepted those files.
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.27-gfj (9f7eb77c3929): Compare the file's raw bytes with what checkout itself would write, `git cat-file --filters <commit>:<rel>` (smudge and EOL conversion applied under this tree's attributes and config). That rejects a file whose only change is its line endings and still accepts a CRLF checkout. Add a variant of un5 that sets core.autocrlf=true, checks out the head, and expects the file to read as the commit's.

findings.issue: The diff writes that `tree_unsettled` is 'the one reading every verb that touches a task tree takes first' and that 'a verb that dispatches into a task tree, integrates it, retires it or moves it asks tree_unsettled first'. The code does not hold that. (a) manage-worktrees.py:700-746 `task-remove` (the `/audit:worktree task-remove` remover of a task tree) never asks. It is not only `--force`, as the executor's outcome says: after a move killed inside its undo, the forced checkout leaves the tree clean, so even the unforced remove passes the dirtiness check, and `git worktree remove` then deletes the admin directory holding the only copy of the work. audit-status.py:2131/2135 prints that remover as the remedy for a kept tree, and retire_member now keeps exactly those trees. (b) drive-phase.py:2223-2250 `resume_writer` opens a writer session in the task tree through `open_dispatch` without going through `dispatch()`, so it never asks either. That path is only reachable if a copy appears after a gate-red-writer decision was parked.
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.28-gfj (f4430d7b8131): Either make the claim true by having manage-worktrees `task-remove` ask `_worktrees.tree_unsettled` and refuse anything but False, forced or not, naming the copy and the restore verb, and by routing `resume_writer` through `unsettled_stop`. Or narrow both sentences to the drive's own dispatch, integration, retirement and move, and file task-remove as a fault. Prefer the first, since the copy is the only record of the work.

findings.issue: Two refusals tell the user that 'the next move drops it': a copy with no index.json, and a copy of a move the marker already recorded (base == end). Both still stand beside the tree, so `unsettled_stop` stops dispatch and integration over them before any move runs. If the drive's next step is integration over a reusable stored green (gate_step skipped, so no advance_member), the stop names `restore`, restore refuses and points at a move, and the next `next` stops again, with no verb that gets out. `_resume` already settles both shapes by dropping the copy.
findings.resolution: In restore_copy, settle both shapes the way `_resume` does: drop the copy (`_drop_copy`) when it has no index.json, or when base == end and `_newer_work` names nothing. Return restored=None with what was dropped instead of a refusal. Add a case for the recorded-move copy, which the executor lists as untested.

findings.issue: The fallback wording ('does not name P') and the case where read_provenance returns a record with a foreign createdBy but a taskId (_worktrees.py:198-201 returns the record) are driven by no case: ta9 only exercises the 'names X, not P' arm, and the executor says so in claim 2. In the foreign-createdBy case the new line reads 'its marker names X, not P' for a marker this plugin did not write, which is true of the taskId field but suggests a plugin marker for another task.
findings.resolution: Add one small over-fire twin of ta9 for a marker with no record (no marker file) asserting the old 'does not name' wording, and optionally gate `named` on rec createdBy so a foreign marker keeps the old wording.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: the task asked to 'set meta.buildCommands.lint through /audit:task build-command (or drop the hand copy and point at verify.sh --list)', and the diff changes only CLAUDE.md:210. The plan still reads `ruff check plugins/audit tools tests && vermin ...` (read at docs/audit/audit-plan.json:24), while tools/verify.sh:589 runs `ruff check plugins/audit tools tests .claude/hooks`. A build-command-driven gate therefore still runs the narrower ruff and misses an unused import under .claude/hooks, which is the class this task closes. findings.issue: The task's own gate selects four suites, and none of them opens CHANGELOG.md or COMPATIBILITY.md. The only matches are message strings that name the document (tests/test__manifest_phases.py:368,379,518 and tests/test__manifest_vocab.py:595); none of them reads the file. So the gate stays green whatever the two edited documents say, including when both new bullets are deleted (an assertion the behaviour never reaches). The suites that do read these documents are outside tests.gate: COMPATIBILITY.md is a BARE path-reference surface at tools/lints/_refs.py:162 (tests/test__refs.py), and _deps.doc_prose_numbers reads both documents (tests/test__deps.py). This is a judgement from reading, not a run. The recorded green says nothing about the edit.
findings.resolution: For a documentation-only task, derive or declare tests.gate from the suites that read the edited documents (tests/test__refs.py and tests/test__deps.py) rather than from the code files scoped in as readers. Alternatively, record in the task that the gate is a regression guard only and that the documents were checked by a direct _deps.doc_prose_numbers(['CHANGELOG.md','COMPATIBILITY.md']) run (it returns 15 on the edited tree, none in the new lines).

findings.issue: documented_rows is unbounded and the basename-alone arm matches any heading naming the bare basename (or, for a declared directory entry, the directory's last component, e.g. 'tests' in '### Adding tests'). The guide paragraph justifies no budget with 'a module rarely has more than one heading', which holds for module files but not for a declared README.md, a directory entry or a generic basename, where the executor brief would grow by one row per heading in every tracked document. Every other brief section is bounded.
findings.resolution: Cap the rows (as _impact.section does for dependants) with an 'N of M shown' tail naming a command that lists all, or skip the basename-alone arm for entries that are directories or have no file extension; add a case with a declared README.md or directory entry.

findings.issue: The diff makes the outputs half of the shared predicate opt-in: declared_git_rels counts outputs only when a caller hands `changed`, and the default `changed=()` silently means files only. drive-phase.py submit_strays calls declared_git_rels in both arms (:9980 bound tree, :9989 serial) without `changed`. That function's docstring says it asks 'the commit's own [question], through the same function on the same basis'. After this diff that is false, and the two readers now disagree on the input this task fixed. In a serial drive, a task that writes a path its own honoured `outputs` covers (ctw-fi2's shape: reports/q3.html under ['reports/**']) gets the plan gate's allow and would get commit-task-work's count and staging. But submit_strays refuses the executor's filing first ('changed reports/q3.html outside its files'), at drive-phase.py:10110-10112. So the end-to-end path the task's tests prove is still unreachable through the driven pipeline, one step before the commit instead of one step after the gate. A bound task tree's member gets told and filed, then left to integration. This is the recurring class again, and it comes from a shared predicate whose second half each caller must remember to switch on. The executor reports it as NOT FIXED, and it is outside the task's files. But it is a caller of the function whose contract this diff changed, so it is charged to the diff.
findings.resolution: fixed in P155.29-gfj (297a0f6aa128): Make the outputs half unskippable, not per-caller. tasks.title: The browser (report) job's live-plan leg stops being killed: the sender is found, the leg's input is bounded, and the job's longest line is a measurement
tasks.description: Closes F816 - three sightings: runs 40913965771 (10-29), 41281241772 and 41308006702 (11-01), each exit 143 about 143 s after "wrote .../live-plan/audit-report.html", inside timeout-minutes 15. Green run 41322244766's browser (report) took 9m05s against ci.yml:103 "longest browser-report: 7m19s (estimate)". No SIGTERM/.kill( sender in check-report-interactive.mjs; verify.sh:208 only relays TERM. Find the sender first (rerun the leg on a ci/ branch with /usr/bin/time -v and runner diagnostics; the orchestrator pushes and dispatches), then bound the live-plan input, then record the measured longest line. The browser gate runs in CI, never in the task tree.

outcome.technical:
SENDER. All four browser (report) failures in the ci.yml runs 40194747670..41349318354 end the same way: the job log reads 'wrote /tmp/verify-*/live-plan/audit-report.html', then two 'Terminated' lines, then '##[error]Process completed with exit code 143.' and '##[error]The runner has received a shutdown signal. This can happen when the runner service is stopped, or a manually started runner is canceled.' Runs/jobs: 40913965771 attempt 1 job 123589129616 (e6f4c0c0, 10-29, killed 171 s after the write), 41212909456 job 124571443610 (f1ad5aad, 10-31, 127 s - a sighting the register did not have), 41281241772 job 124773437950 (438838a0, 165 s), 41308006702 job 124852303910 (a5c8d566, 143 s). So the SIGTERM comes from the runner: its listener got a shutdown signal and stopped the step's processes. It is not the job timeout (that ends the job as cancelled with a max-execution-time message, and every failure ended between 3m40s and 4m23s, inside 15 minutes), and it is not our code (no SIGTERM or kill sender in check-report-interactive.mjs; verify.sh only passes TERM on). WHY the runner shut down cannot be read from these logs. Hosted runners do not expose dmesg after the fact, and check-report-interactive buffers its output, so the log does not show which check was running when the job died. SAME DEFECT AS BUG-32: very likely, but not proven. For: all four killed SHAs lack 12937474 (git merge-base --is-ancestor: e6f4c0c0, f1ad5aad, 438838a0 and a5c8d566 lack it; fa1b0c81 has it). At those SHAs the live-plan leg calls page.pdf twice, portrait and landscape, over one table that spans the whole plan (check-report-interactive.mjs:2132 at a5c8d566). BUG-32 shows that same page failing printToPDF locally, and its own 'actual' field names run 41281241772 as the CI form of it. Both browser (report) jobs that ran after the fix passed: 41322244766 (9m05s) and the main push 41349318354 (7m53s). Against: the pre-fix code also passed on the same kind of input, for example 40913965771 attempt 2 on the very SHA its attempt 1 died on (5m56s), and 41210168802/41215763718 on 10-31 (8m53s, 8m26s). So the kill is intermittent, which fits memory pressure close to the VM's limit better than a fixed 'Printing failed'. Two green samples after the fix are weak evidence against a failure rate that ran at three of the last four pre-fix runs. The 10-29 sighting is the same shape: it predates 12937474 and was printing the same single-table page. WHAT REMAINS AFTER THE FIX, AND WHAT CHANGED: (1) tools/verify.sh rendered_plan_legs now renders a WINDOW of docs/audit/audit-plan.json instead of the whole plan. An inline python heredoc, written like the one-status leg's, writes $WORKDIR/live-window. It keeps every phase that is not done, the 20 most recent done phases, every phase carrying a top-level phase or task key or status that no kept phase carries, and every phase that kept phase/task blockedBy/dependsOn references point into. It copies the shards untouched, narrows fileIndex, bugs and proposals to what was kept, and prints 'live plan window: K of N phases, k of n tasks'. validate-manifest then runs on the window before render-report. On this tree it printed 'live plan window: 47 of 158 phases, 610 of 1439 tasks' twice, validate-manifest said OK, and the rendered report is 3899168 bytes against 10749127 for the whole plan. The output name is still audit-report.html, so the aged step's "$lp/audit-report.html" and the --stress-print call are unchanged. The stress print is bounded already (STRESS_PRINT_PX fixed, STRESS_BOUND_MS 300 s), so it covers the print-crash length whatever size the window is. The window now grows only with the phases not done and the references the kept phases make. vermin -t=3.8- on the extracted code: minimum 3.0, rc 0; sh -n tools/verify.sh rc 0. (2) .github/workflows/ci.yml: the browser-report longest line is now the measurement '9m05s (run 41322244766, 15:38:30 to 15:47:35)', the longest finished browser (report) job of the 36 non-skipped attempts across the 39 runs from 40194747670 to 41349318354, enumerated with gh api .../runs/<id>/attempts/<n>/jobs. timeout-minutes moves 15 -> 19, the first whole minute at or above 2 x 9m05s = 18m10s and under the 3x ceiling of 27m15s. The estimate list now says browser-report is measured and asks for a re-measure on the first run of the windowed shape. (3) CONTRIBUTING.md: the report-slice paragraph says the leg renders a window and points at rendered_plan_legs and the printed line. Gates: python3 tools/gate-parity.py rc 0; sh tools/verify.sh --list rc 0, and its output equals HEAD's copy except the version lines, which differ only because HEAD's copy ran from the scratch directory; _deps.doc_prose_numbers() reports nothing in CONTRIBUTING.md. No browser gate was run (machine-wide lock). DEPENDANTS: tools/verify.sh's (.gitattributes, ci.yml, derive-phase-gate.py, test__output.py, test__refs.py, affected.py, check-example-pins.py, check-git-pipeline.py, and the rest): still correct. They name verify.sh by path or read its slices, and the slice set is unchanged. tools/check-report-interactive.mjs: not edited, so its dependants are unchanged; its header's /tmp/live-plan/*.html glob still names $lp. .github/workflows/ci.yml's: still correct. No job, job name, slice or matrix changed, only one timeout and comments; gate-parity is green and job_bound_evidence reads the new line (shown both ways above). tools/gate-parity.py, tools/lints/_deps.py, tools/prove-gates.py, tools/sweep-selftests.py, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, stamp-verification.py, tests/_harness.py, test__deps.py, test__runner_collects.py, test_stamp_verification.py, test__affected_tests.py, test__doctor_trail.py, test_drive_phase.py: declared but not edited. None of them pins the edited text: a grep for 'live plan', live-plan, rendered_plan_legs, 'timeout-minutes: 15', 7m19s and browser-report over tests/, tools/*.py, tools/lints and plugins/audit/scripts found only unrelated 'live plan' prose. The orchestrator's sweep is the verdict on them. tools/check-rendered-artifacts.py: renders the committed reports, not the live plan, so unaffected. FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR - the CI that settles what this tree cannot: (A) push the phase branch with this change to ci/P155 and dispatch: gh workflow run ci.yml --ref ci/P155, then gh run view <id> --json jobs --jq '.jobs[]|select(.name=="browser (report)")|[.conclusion,.startedAt,.completedAt]'. Settled when browser (report) is success and its log carries 'live plan window: ...' and 'report is interactive: N checks passed in /tmp/verify-*/live-plan/audit-report.html'. Its duration then replaces the 9m05s line, and the bound comes down to the first whole minute at or above twice it, never below 5. (B) optional, to name WHY the runner shut down: a throwaway branch ci/diag-f816 at a5c8d566 (a known-killed SHA) whose browser-report 'verify slice' step reads: run: |
  ( while :; do printf 'MEM %s ' "$(date -u +%T)"; free -m | awk '/^Mem:/{print "used",$3,"avail",$7}'; sleep 3; done ) &
  ( sudo dmesg -w 2>/dev/null | grep -i --line-buffered -E 'oom|killed process' | sed 's/^/KERN /' ) &
  sh tools/verify.sh --only report. Dispatch it two or three times (the kill is intermittent). The samplers stream into the step's own log, so they survive a shutdown that skips every later step. Settled as memory exhaustion if 'avail' falls toward zero, or a KERN oom line appears, just before 'Terminated'; refuted if avail stays high up to the shutdown. Never merge that branch.
outcome.descriptive: The SIGTERM is the hosted runner shutting the job down. It hit only SHAs before the BUG-32 fix, inside the live-plan leg that was printing one whole-plan table, so it is very likely BUG-32. The leg now renders a bounded window of the live plan (47 of 158 phases today), and the browser-report bound rests on the measured 9m05s, raised to 19 minutes.

tasks.title: A task commit's Co-Authored-By names the model that wrote the work, or nothing
tasks.description: Closes F804. Evidence at fa1b0c81: _scoped_commit.py:1069-1077 coauthor_of returns meta.commit.coauthor; commit-task-work.py:835,1610 take it. Derive the trailer from the executor's recorded model for that start; keep reading meta.commit.coauthor as the fallback (COMPATIBILITY.md: a key the plugin reads keeps being read); omit the trailer when nothing is recorded. State the drive's own state-commit trailer rule explicitly.

outcome.technical: Trailer source moved from configuration to the usage ledger. commit-task-work.py: new recorded_models(rows, task_id, started_at) - the model ids of ledger rows labelled `attr: task` for the task, whose agentType is the plugin's executor (`audit-executor` after any plugin namespace), at the start's hour bucket or later, usage_ledger.is_model_id true, `:long-prompt` tier suffix dropped, each once, sorted; no start moment -> []. executor_models(project, config, task) reads the ledger at hooks/_config.ledger_dir(project, config) (the metering hook's own reading) via usage_ledger.read_ledger(since=start date); a ledger that cannot be read is [] (no trailer, no claim). coauthor_note() adds a `degraded:` line when the plan asks for a trailer and none is recorded. message_parts(task_id, subject, manifest, models=()) now returns _scoped_commit.task_coauthor(manifest, models). The --state commit passes no co-author at all (comment states the rule: it carries the plan's record, written by the plugin's verbs, so no model is its author). _scoped_commit.py: COAUTHOR_TRAILER = 'Co-Authored-By: %s <noreply@anthropic.com>' and task_coauthor(manifest, models) - one line per model in one paragraph, None when the plan's meta.commit.coauthor is unset/blank (absence keeps meaning no trailer) or nothing is recorded; coauthor_of stays the one reading of the key, docstring updated. New import edge commit-task-work -> usage_ledger (an entry point reading a lower layer); PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md module-map line updated to match `python3 tools/lints/_deps.py --render` (map_drift() -> []). DIVERGENCE FROM THE BRIEF'S WORD 'fallback', stated: meta.commit.coauthor is still read, but as the plan asking for a trailer, not as the trailer text when nothing is recorded - F804's own Do says never from a configured constant, the orchestrator's note says nothing recorded is no trailer, and COMPATIBILITY.md's absence rule forbids a record starting to write trailers onto plans that never set the key; a text fallback would re-issue the exact false claim F804 records whenever the ledger has no row. Docs in scope: COMPATIBILITY.md (meta.commit.coauthor bullet under manifest keys: still read, absence still no trailer, set value's text no longer written, --state carries none), plugins/audit/reference/config.md (new `usage.ledgerDir` section stating the task-commit rule and the drive's own state-commit rule: no trailer on --state after a block, at sign-off, at a landing), PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (commit-task-work section paragraph + map edge). Tests: test_commit_task_work.py new staged block co-block (_coauthor_cases, co1-co7) added to STAGES; ctw28 and the 571becfd literal case updated to pass models and expect the derived trailer (they pinned the configured line as the trailer, which is the defect). tasks.title: A task tree is unsettled by one predicate every verb reads, the stop names a restore verb, and the move's byte comparison bypasses filters
tasks.description: Closes F805. Evidence at fa1b0c81: git/_worktrees.py:2112 hash-object without --no-filters; the only restore verb is drive-phase.restore_carry (:5920), from the carry ref, not from the kept copy. One shared "unsettled" predicate read by dispatch, integration, retirement and advance_member.

add: tests/test__worktrees.py: retire refuses while a kept copy exists; _reads_as rejects a file differing only in line endings (hash-object --no-filters); a restore verb restores from <copy>/N.bin plus git-index
gate: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__worktrees.py tests/test_drive_phase.py tests/test_integrate_task.py tools/_suite.py

outcome.technical:
CHANGES.
plugins/audit/scripts/git/_worktrees.py: (a) `tree_unsettled(tree, run=None, now=None)` -> {unsettled True|False|None, kept, why, cleared}: the one reading of whether a move's copy (admin_dir/audit-advance) or its tombstone stands beside a task tree, read through the same `_left_beside` every move's `kept` uses; None (could-not-ask, never settled) when git will not name the admin dir; `why` is `kept_where()`, which names <copy>/N.bin, <copy>/index.json and <copy>/git-index. (b) `_clear_strays`: the `.audit-*` temp files `_write_aside` leaves in the admin dir after a hard kill are removed by tree_unsettled once older than STRAY_AGE_SECONDS (a younger one may be a write in flight and is left); `_write_aside` now takes its prefix from STRAY_PREFIX (same value). (c) `restore_copy(tree, task_id, is_record=None, run=None)` -> {restored True|False|None, kept, paths, error}: puts the tree back at the copy's `from` from N.bin + git-index through `_undo` and its `_answers_as` check, drops the copy; refuses with nothing written when the marker does not name the task at the copy's base (a recorded move: the next move drops it), the copy has no index.json or will not read, or `_newer_work` names a path the copy does not hold; None when no copy stands (a tombstone alone is cleared). (d) `_reads_as` hashes with `hash-object --no-filters`; its docstring states the cost (under core.autocrlf, a moved file a killed checkout already wrote reads as differing, so a resumed move holds instead of finishing). Module docstring: writes git in two places now (advance_tree, restore_copy).
plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py: `unsettled_stop(ctx, task, tree)` and `unsettled_said(...)` (stop names the copy's files and `restore_command()` = `python3 <drive-phase.py> restore <id> <manifest> --project-dir <project>`); read by `dispatch` (when a tree is given), `integrate_member` (before integrating), `remove_task_tree` (first check, so retirement and both kept-tree removers refuse while a copy or tombstone stands) and `advance_member` (re-reads the predicate after the move; could-not-ask there stays the move's own tree-not-moved decision). A tree directory that is gone is no stop in unsettled_stop (the verb refuses it by name; retire_member runs no removal for it). New subcommand `restore <taskId> [manifest] [--project-dir DIR]` (`run_restore`/`restore_tree`): tree from the drive state's wave.trees, records from member_records, under the phase lock (released unless a drive held it before); exit 0 restored, 1 refused (copy stays), 2 no tree / no copy. Usage and exit-code docstring updated.
tests/test__worktrees.py: un1-un8 in a new `_unsettled_cases` (called from _advance_crash_cases); calls to the new functions go through `_asked`, so a module without them fails the case instead of raising. tests/test_drive_phase.py: ab9 (after ab8: stop names <copy>/git-index and the restore command; `main(["restore", ...])` exit 0, copy gone, work bytes back; the next `next` integrates the member) and uv1 (`_unsettled_verb_cases`: dispatch and integrate_member stop over a copy without running their verb, and go on with the copy gone). PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: a paragraph in the _worktrees section and a sentence in drive-phase's 'A wave's edges'.

TDD ORDER AND RED. Tests drafted first; I read only the test file and the function names/signatures of _worktrees (plus remove_task_tree, which is where the retire seam is) before writing them. First run on unfixed code: `python3 tests/test__worktrees.py --selftest` -> exit 1, 156/164, FAIL un1..un8 by assertion (un4 printed (True, '', ...): today's remover deleted the tree with its copy; un5 printed (True, True): the filtered hash accepted the CRLF file). Against HEAD's code in a scratch `git archive HEAD` export with my two test files copied over (never the shared tree): test__worktrees 156/164 with un1-un8 FAIL; test_drive_phase --stage ab-block 9/10 with ab9 FAIL (argparse: invalid choice 'restore'). uv1 was written after and is proved by mutation rows m13/m14/m15 below and by the submit helper's run.

GATE (own-tests: the sweep command the brief names). First run: exit 1 - ar12, wc1, wc2 (test_drive_phase) and _suite s23 red, all from my change: the could-not-ask stop fired over a tree that is gone or fake, and a bare shutil.rmtree in my test. Fixed in my files (gone-directory guard in unsettled_stop; advance_member stops on `is True`; _harness.remove_tree). Second run: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__worktrees.py tests/test_drive_phase.py tests/test_integrate_task.py tools/_suite.py` -> exit 0, '4/4 files ok, 1023 cases'. After a later one-line test edit (un3's cleanup made tolerant), `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__worktrees.py` -> 164 cases ok. `python3 tools/check-git-pipeline.py` was NOT run (the brief's own-tests reading names only the sweep). Development checks, not gates: ruff check on the four .py files -> 'All checks passed!'; vermin -t=3.8- on them -> exit 0; house_style_violations / prose_number_claims / doc_prose_numbers -> no hit in the touched files.

MUTATION PROBE: <scratchpad>/p15512/mutations.py - usage: `python3 <scratchpad>/p15512/mutations.py [--repo CHECKOUT] [--only ID,...] [--jobs N]` from the checkout (copies the tracked files as on disk into a scratch tree per row, asserts the anchor occurs exactly once, purges __pycache__). Run: 16 rows; the full run killed 14 and reported m9 ANCHOR-MISSING (my anchor was wrong); after fixing the anchor and un3's cleanup, `--only m4,m9` killed both -> every row killed: m1 retire skips predicate->un4; m2 always unsettled->un1,un3,un4; m3 could-not-ask as settled->un2; m4 any age cleared->un3; m5 never cleared->un3; m6 filters back->un5; m7 never matches->un5,av39; m8 restore over newer work->un7; m9 refuse own paths->un6; m10 no git-index->un6; m11 no copy reads restored->un8; m12 stop without verb->ab9,uv1; m13 dispatch skips->uv1; m14 integration skips->uv1; m15 stop on every tree->ab1-ab9,uv1; m16 verb unwired->ab9.

DEPENDANTS. _worktrees.py (guard-release.py, close-phase.py, integrate-task.py, manage-worktrees.py, _evidence_io.py, drive-phase.py, run-test-gate.py, stamp-verification.py): still correct - only names were added and `import time`; `_reads_as` is private and its one caller is `_newer_work` in the same module (grep found no other reader); `_write_aside`'s prefix value is unchanged; `_place`, `_keep_copy`, `_put`, `_read_copy` untouched. BUT the class lives on in two files outside this task: manage-worktrees.py task-remove (~line 740) runs `git worktree remove [--force]` on a task tree without asking tree_unsettled, so `--force` still deletes a copy with the admin directory; and audit-status.py (~line 2131) prints `git worktree remove --force <path>` as a kept tree's remedy. Neither was edited (not in files). drive-phase.py (test__filed_returns, test__invariants, test_audit_status, test_commit_task_work, test_detect_plan_skip, test_stamp_verification, tools/stream-cost.py, test_drive_phase): the names they use (_advance_plan, _attempt_start_moment, _carries, _close_plan, ...) are unchanged; the new checks return a stop only for an existing tree directory with a copy or tombstone beside it, or could-not-ask - none of those suites was run here (own-tests). test__worktrees.py (.github/sweep-costs.json, tools/affected.py): _cases/_selftest unchanged; the suite gains cases so its recorded cost is now low (not re-recorded; the sweep measured it at 32.3s). test_drive_phase.py (sweep-costs.json, ci.yml, test__runner_output, test_run_test_gate, test_stamp_verification, tools/affected.py, tools/reach-diff.py): STAGES unchanged; ab-block gains ab9 and uv1, so its recorded cost is low too. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: paragraphs added, nothing renamed; the doc prose lint is clean.

DOCUMENTS OUTSIDE MY FILES. No sentence I found became false: no command or agent document lists drive-phase's subcommands beyond submit/brief/next, and no document described the old 'until a human has read the copy' stop. CHANGELOG.md carries no entry for this change (not in files).

ORCHESTRATOR NOTES. The post-setup conflict dry run in recut_conflicts does not belong in this predicate: tree_unsettled asks one thing about the disk (does a move's copy stand beside a tree), and a recut's conflict dry run asks whether a patch applies over a head - different inputs, different answer. I did not touch the redo pin settler or recut_conflicts. Not tested: restore refusing when another session holds the phase lock (take_lock's stop path), and restore of a move the marker recorded (the refusal is written, no case drives it).

But the document records every earlier exit-code move on an audit-task verb 'because an exit code moved from 0 to 2 on a shipped command, and a pipeline that read ... is a pipeline that now stops' (COMPATIBILITY.md:546-556). The repo's precedent P153-R3 filed the missing CHANGELOG line for a `--gate*` behaviour change as a finding. tasks.title: fix P155-R9: The commit's count of 'declared' got wider, but what it stages d...
tasks.description:
The commit's count of 'declared' got wider, but what it stages did not. owned_rels now counts every fileIndex row keyed to the committing task. stage_targets still stages only task.files (commit-task-work.py:355-376). So a changed path that only a fileIndex row of the task names lands in undeclared_changes' `covered` (_scoped_commit.py:1507-1514). The commit treats it as work in flight: it does not refuse it and does not stage it. The file stays dirty and the task closes `done` without it. Before this diff the commit refused that path by name; now it drops it in silence, the outcome attempt_refusal's own docstring says it exists to prevent. The validator allows such rows: _manifest_crossrefs._check_file_index only requires files to be a subset of fileIndex, not the reverse. dp1 asserts the commit 'counts' src/indexed.py but never asserts the path is committed. Found by reading, not by a run.

Resolution asked: Treat `files` alone as declared. fileIndex is derived from files (`audit-task.py reindex`), so a row present only in fileIndex is drift: declared_task_map should not read fileIndex rows that no counted task's files covers. The hook then denies more, never less. Update dp1's expected list (src/indexed.py is neither opened nor counted). If fileIndex rows must stay, stage_targets has to stage every declared_task_map entry of the committing task. Either way, add a case: a path only the committing task's fileIndex row names is committed or refused, never left dirty after `done`.

outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: recut_tree now checks the work again in the recut tree after executor.worktreeSetup has run, and applies it there, through the new apply_in_recut. It runs the scratch-index conflict check over that tree's own index (git write-tree, then recut_conflicts), and only then the real three-way apply, which git makes whole or not at all. A refusal there is undone by the new undo_recut: the recut tree goes through remove_task_tree (the only remover), with what it holds now as carried, since it was cut under the lock and holds only what the setup wrote. Then the drive state snapshot taken before keep_old_tree is restored, then the old tree's original marker, in that order so a crash between them is settled by settle_kept_markers. Then drop_redo_work removes the patch and pin, and the redo is refused by name with the old tree, work, base and carry ref unchanged. If the undo stops part way, the existing after_kept stop naming the kept patch still applies. The recut_conflicts docstring claimed 'the recut tree is a fresh checkout of head, so this answers for it', which was false under a setup; it now says it answers for the bare head only. The recut_tree and remove_task_tree docstrings and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (the redo paragraph and the one-remover paragraph) are updated. DEVIATION FROM THE LITERAL RESOLUTION: the new tree cannot be cut before the old one is kept. manage-worktrees.py task-add adopts any tree whose marker names the task (manage-worktrees.py:603-614), and rewriting that marker is the keeping. So the order is: keep, cut with setup, check there, and undo the keep on refusal. The end state is the same as a refusal made before the keep, and that end state is what ar3s asserts. Doing it literally would need manage-worktrees.py, which is outside this task's files. tests/test_drive_phase.py: _ab_red_at_base and _ar_at_decision take setup=, passed to _wave_repo. New _recut_setup_cases is called from _recut_refused_move_cases (stage ar-block) and adds two cases. ar3s: a setup that rewrites src/f1.txt only where fixed.txt exists (the head, never the first cut). The redo is refused naming src/f1.txt; afterwards the old tree is wave.trees' entry with its marker naming P1.1 again, HEAD at base, work bytes, carry ref and wave.bases unchanged, git worktree list the same as before the redo, no gate rows, no patch, no refs/audit/redo pin, and the decision still stands. ar3t is the over-fire twin: a setup that writes nothing, and the redo recuts, gates green at head and closes on the merged bytes. Mutations, each made and restored in one script in this tree with __pycache__ purged: marker restore removed -> ar3s FAIL (8/9); state restore removed -> ar3s FAIL (8/9); undo replaced by a fixed failure -> ar3s FAIL (8/9); apply_in_recut always refusing -> ar2, ar2b, ar3s, ar3t, ar4 FAIL (4/9). Gate runs: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py -> '1/1 files ok, 806 cases', exit 0. python3 tools/prove-gates.py --selftest -> 'ALL PASS: 66/66 cases passed', exit 0. ruff check and vermin -t=3.8- on both .py files are clean; prose_number_claims, doc_prose_numbers and house_style_violations have no hits on the touched files. DEPENDANTS: tests importing drive-phase.py (test__filed_returns, test__invariants, test__worktrees, test_audit_status, test_commit_task_work, test_detect_plan_skip, test_stamp_verification) are still correct. No signature or return shape changed: keep_old_tree still returns {key, path} (ta22 pins this), recut_conflicts keeps its signature (its head argument may now also be a tree object), and only two functions were added. tools/stream-cost.py is still correct: no new journal action. undo_recut writes a did-line, not a journal row. The task.worktree row add_tree wrote for the undone tree stays as history. Path dependants of test_drive_phase.py (sweep-costs.json, ci.yml, affected.py, reach-diff.py, test_run_test_gate.py, test__runner_output.py, test_stamp_verification.py) are still correct: no stage was added or renamed, and the new cases run inside the existing ar-block stage. That stage takes about 26s locally, so .github/sweep-costs.json may under-weigh ar-block, which is a re-record question, not breakage. The PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md basename dependants are unaffected: no heading or anchor was renamed. F808 is in the private register, which this task cannot edit; whether it closes is the orchestrator's call, with the deviation above.

tasks.title: fix P155-R16: The window is written to $WORKDIR/live-window/audit-plan.json, ...
tasks.description:
The window is written to $WORKDIR/live-window/audit-plan.json, outside any checkout, so render-report resolves its project through _output.project_of_manifest to /tmp/verify-*/live-window (markerless fallback; checked in memory: project_of_manifest('/tmp/verify-XYZ/live-window/audit-plan.json') -> '/tmp/verify-XYZ/live-window'). The committed evidence ledger (docs/audit/evidence) is then never read. Measured in memory with _evidence_view.load_evidence on the same manifest: at the checkout path, keys ['passed','failed','empty-gate','no-evidence'], flags ['tree-mutated','tree-unknown','no-overlap','coverage-unknown','checks-unknown'], files 60. At the window path, keys ['dangling','no-evidence'], flags [], files 0. So the leg now drives a report where every pointer is 'dangling', a status the real plan never shows, and it loses every real evidence status and flag. That was what made the live-plan leg the report that 'DOES carry evidence' (tools/check-report-interactive.mjs:766-770). Nothing goes red: validate-manifest passes and the browser check accepts either page. The new comment ('the page still shows each key and status the plan uses') and CONTRIBUTING.md:503-504 overclaim for the same reason. The project's .claude/audit.config.json (theme and panel config) is also no longer read.

Resolution asked: Give the window a project the renderer resolves the way it resolves the checkout. Write it under a record-shaped path, $WORKDIR/live-window/docs/audit/audit-plan.json, so the project is $WORKDIR/live-window. Copy docs/audit/evidence/ (and .claude/audit.config.json) beside it. Then make the drift fail: after the render, assert that the window's load_evidence keys and flags equal the full plan's (or, at minimum, contain no 'dangling' the full plan lacks) and fail the leg otherwise.

gate: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/_harness.py tests/test__affected_tests.py tests/test__runner_collects.py tests/test_stamp_verification.py

outcome.technical: tools/verify.sh: the live-plan window step moved out of rendered_plan_legs into a new POSIX function live_plan_window DIR. It writes the window at DIR/docs/audit/audit-plan.json, the plan's own record-shaped path, with its shards beside it. It copytrees docs/audit/evidence into DIR/docs/audit/evidence and copies .claude/audit.config.json into DIR/.claude/. As a result _output.project_of_manifest(window) is DIR, checked in lw1. The shape closure now also keeps any phase whose task or phase evidence status or flag (read by _evidence_view.load_evidence with _evidence_io.boundary_for, as render-report.py reads it) no kept phase carries. Without that arm the window lost 'empty-gate', 'tree-unknown' and 'coverage-unknown'. After writing, the step reads the evidence of the full plan and of the window and exits 1 if either reading is absent alone, if the keys or flags chip lists differ, or if any task or phase-own view the window keeps has a different (status, flags). tasks.title: fix P155-R20: restore_copy can write over newer work at a path the copy holds...
tasks.description:
restore_copy can write over newer work at a path the copy holds. It drops every path in `held` from `_newer_work`'s answer (`[p for p in _newer_work(...) if p not in held]`), and `_undo` then `_put`s each held path unconditionally. Suppose a.txt is a held work path and, after the kill, someone (a human, or a writer session that was already running) edits it to bytes that are neither the copy's nor `start`'s nor `end`'s. The restore overwrites that edit without saying so. un7 covers only an unheld path (c.txt), so this direction has no test. The docstring narrows the contract to 'the paths it holds are what a restore is asked to write over', which conflicts with 'never write over newer work'.

Resolution asked: Before `_undo`, refuse any held path whose bytes match none of these: the copy (`_holds(tree, rel, held[rel])`), `start`'s blob, or `end`'s blob (`_reads_as`, absent where the commit has none). Those are the only states a killed move or a killed undo can leave. un6's tree (a.txt at base, n.txt absent) still passes. Add a case like un7 that edits a.txt and expects a refusal with nothing changed.

tasks.title: fix P155-R21: `hash-object --no-filters` costs more than the docstring says. ...
tasks.description:
`hash-object --no-filters` costs more than the docstring says. With core.autocrlf=true, the Git for Windows installer default, every text file checkout writes with CRLF hashes differently from its LF blob. So a move killed partway through its checkout leaves moved paths that `_newer_work` reads as newer work. The resume holds the tree, and so does the restore verb the new stop names: restore_copy runs the same `_newer_work` and refuses those paths, because moved paths are not in `held`. On a default Windows checkout, the stop's sentence '`restore` puts the work back from it and takes it down' is then false and no verb can settle the tree. The filtered hash this replaces accepted those files.

Resolution asked: Compare the file's raw bytes with what checkout itself would write, `git cat-file --filters <commit>:<rel>` (smudge and EOL conversion applied under this tree's attributes and config). That rejects a file whose only change is its line endings and still accepts a CRLF checkout. Add a variant of un5 that sets core.autocrlf=true, checks out the head, and expects the file to read as the commit's.

(b) drive-phase.py:2223-2250 `resume_writer` opens a writer session in the task tree through `open_dispatch` without going through `dispatch()`, so it never asks either. That path is only reachable if a copy appears after a gate-red-writer decision was parked.

Resolution asked: Either make the claim true by having manage-worktrees `task-remove` ask `_worktrees.tree_unsettled` and refuse anything but False, forced or not, naming the copy and the restore verb, and by routing `resume_writer` through `unsettled_stop`. Or narrow both sentences to the drive's own dispatch, integration, retirement and move, and file task-remove as a fault. Prefer the first, since the copy is the only record of the work.

tasks.description:
The recurring class: the plan gate, the commit, the drive's submit and the close each read "declared" and they disagree on a task's honoured outputs. Route submit_strays (both arms) and _uncommitted_leftovers (others and mine's outputs arm) through it. Fix the docstrings it makes false (submit_strays, _uncommitted_leftovers), and bring reference/orchestrator.md step 4c in line with what the commit stages (R30).

Prove it: a drive-phase case where a serial task writing a path its honoured outputs cover is filed, not refused, with a second-direction twin where a stray beside it still is; an audit-task case where commit-task-work commits with a sibling's output path dirty and done --commit closes without the "no in_progress task declaring it" refusal, with a twin for a stray no pattern covers. Add one case that fails if a caller of the predicate is added that reads files alone (a structural pin over the readers), where feasible.

outcome.technical: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]: Added gains three entries (the new `drive-phase.py restore <taskId>` verb with its refusals and exit codes; the triage `--answer leave --fix <ids> --reason`; the executor brief's `Where your files are documented` section). The existing `audit-task start` reader-refusal entry is extended with what the phase narrowed and added: only readers inside the edited region, `scope --files +` answers not asked again, and `--introduces delete:/rename:` asking for importers. Changed gains the four R43 entries: the Co-Authored-By trailer names the model the ledger recorded, the configured text is never written, and --state commits carry none; /audit:worktree task-remove and remove --path refuse a tree with a move's copy beside it, --force included, and the drive and /audit:status name the restore command; a task commit stages the changed paths its own outputs patterns cover; the plan gate no longer opens an edit through a fileIndex row alone. Changed also gains entries for the other shipped behaviour I found by reading git log 531fe6ec..HEAD and each task outcome in P155.json: submit refuses an undeclared edit on the serial path, and scope-changed re-runs the gate before close; the drive runs a ready task before it re-offers a triage or sign-off, drops a member that is no longer ready, and writes the brief for a verb-started task; run-test-gate --task's walk arm and the test-support widening settled by an unscoped declared entry; the red-first helper and test-support modules. A new Fixed section covers: HEAD read one way (empty loose ref, pathspec shapes, start-head tie); the hooks' git-place memo and the same-second arm/revoke; the autocrlf move comparison; a redo undone when the recut setup refuses, plus redo pins dropped; and the kept-tree refusal naming the marker's task. Left out as not shipped to plugin users: the tools/, CI, test-suite and repository-doc tasks (release.py, the plan window, the cost table, ruff over .claude/hooks, prove-gates renames, the AST pins). COMPATIBILITY.md: the coauthor promise was already recorded and is unchanged. Added a 'forced removal of a task tree with a move's copy beside it - and it changed' bullet among the exit-code moves outside the promise (exit 0 -> 1, repair is the restore verb). tasks.description: CI run 41616818469 (release tier, fdf3b270), windows legs: gate-parity lw1 fails - code=1 project=None, out '/usr/bin/dash: 1: C:\hostedtoolcache\...\python3.exe: not found'. gate: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/_harness.py tests/test__affected_tests.py tests/test__runner_collects.py tests/test_stamp_verification.py

outcome.technical: Cause: lw1 handed dash sys.executable as a native Windows path made only of backslashes. A POSIX shell looks up a command name containing no slash on PATH, so dash printed 'not found'. Fix in tools/gate-parity.py: (1) new shell_spelled(path, sep=None), which returns the path unchanged when the separator is '/' and otherwise swaps the separator for '/'. That forward-slash form is what verify.sh gets from cygpath -m for a native program, and the same sys.executable.replace('\\','/') spelling the suites in tests/ already give Git Bash (test_stamp_verification's git filter, test_drive_phase's gate commands).
